proof_summary: Digit-by-digit induction, including the carries created by multiplication by 5, shows that complementing an integer by \(q\mapsto 10^L-1-q\) negates the digit-sum difference \(s(5q)-s(q)\), so the corresponding signed terms cancel in pairs. Since \(2m_k+1=10^k-1\), the terms immediately outward from the center are such complementary pairs, and induction on the distance from the center gives equality of the two partial sums.
